prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: production sprite atlas for Cosmic: A Sea Beneath the Moon. Input image1 is a STYLE reference only: retain the medallion form, palette, grain and physical depiction approach, but create the NEW requested subjects below. Exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, 16 circles total. Regular equal square cells, Use a SQUARE canvas, exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, equal square cells, no outer margin. Aim2048px wide. Every circle diameter84%of its cell, centred, with generous fully transparent gutters; leave allcells complete and separated. No extra cells or objects. Original astronomical chromolithograph with dry-gouache and chalk masses: deep indigo circular fields, feathered warm-ivory light, amber heat, copper/charcoal minerals and restrained teal water. Simplify to broad meaningful structures visible at72px. Fine grain stays in subjects; generous quiet dark space. One thin ivory circular outline. No glossy UI buttons, photographic lens flare, ornamental decoration, humans, machines, text, labels, numerals, formulas or grid lines. Inside each circle the field is opaque; outside circles true alpha transparency. No shadows, rays or fragments beyond circles. Atom/particle diagrams are schematic: tiny compact ivory dots and diffuse electron-probability clouds, never planetary electron orbits; individual nuclei do NOT glow like stars. Exact invisible chemistry is communicated by game names/readings, never by invented diagnostic coloration. All terrestrial worlds have bare mineral terrain; no plants, life or modern continents. Early Moon is pale gray-ivory without familiar dark maria. All Earth cutaways are views of one continuing world.
Strict row-major subjects (left to right, then top to bottom):
1. A rocky body’s gravity: A small rocky sphere with sparse inward radial cues and one short curving external trajectory. Avoid: A gravitational-field convention; no magnetic pole lines or funnel.
2. Gravitational focusing: A rocky body bends two passing small-body paths toward its surface, with widely separated incoming tracks. Avoid: Paths curve because of the body; no already completed impact.
3. Gravity around a growing outer core: A substantial dark core draws a broad surrounding faint gas veil inward with two sparse cues. Avoid: Gas capture around an outer core; no dense established envelope yet.
4. A dispersing gas disk: A broad faint solar-disk arc with large gaps and wisps fading outward, the central Sun small. Avoid: Overall gas depletion, not bipolar cavities or a shattered solid ring.
5. A later-growing outer core: A modest rock-and-volatile core sits in a sparse fading gas arc, a few small solids nearby. Avoid: Timing supplied by sparse disk context; no unique surface colour for lateness.
6. A growing rock-and-ice core: An irregular rounded dark core accretes a few pale ice-bearing small bodies, little gas yet. Avoid: Rock-and-volatile assembly; do not show a permanently frozen interior.
7. A core holding a gas envelope: The same outer core sits inside a large faint translucent spherical gas veil, core still clearly visible. Avoid: Loose extended envelope rather than an opaque finished gas giant.
8. A cooling, contracting envelope: The same core's gas envelope is tighter and denser, with two faint radiation strokes leaving its edge. Avoid: Energy-loss contraction; core still suggested through cutaway, no solid atmospheric shell.
9. A gas giant: A large softly banded warm ivory and ochre gas sphere, broad cloudy bands and subdued edge shading. Avoid: No star rays, terrestrial surface, familiar Great Red Spot or required Saturn rings.
10. A late core rich in rock and volatiles: A rounded outer core in cutaway with a broad heavy-material interior and a very thin surrounding gas veil. Avoid: Heavy composition is schematic; no thick frozen blue ice layer claimed.
11. An ice-giant-like world: A smaller softly shaded muted blue-gray world with a restrained atmosphere and faint broad cloud bands. Avoid: No exposed snow surface; colour is illustrative atmosphere, not evidence of an ice mantle.
12. Small bodies scattered by a giant: A gas giant at one side bends several small-body tracks into diverging inward and outward routes. Avoid: Some paths leave, some turn inward; no guaranteed delivery to Earth.
13. Crossing planetary orbits: Two incomplete curved orbital tracks intersect, each carrying one small rocky body well before the crossing. Avoid: Actual path intersection, no decorative atom-like orbits or collision flash.
14. Accreting planetary embryos: Two unequal rounded rocky embryos each receive a few smaller bodies, separated across the medallion. Avoid: Several growing bodies, not two finished Earth copies.
15. A strongly attracting embryo: One dominant rounded rocky embryo curves nearby small-body paths toward itself, subordinate debris around it. Avoid: A growing selected body; Earth identity not yet established.
16. A rocky proto-Earth: A single charcoal rocky sphere with amber seams and an asymmetric broad dark basalt region, a few accreting rock fragments. Avoid: Establish Earth's body proportions; no ocean, atmosphere, vegetation or continents.
